The user wants the photo to say "Welcome to our sale!" with accurate lip sync. The talking-photo tool needs an audio file I don't have and doesn't generate speech, so the spoken-ad tool, which turns a script into speech over the image, is the direct fit. I can't promise every word will sync perfectly, and it runs on the free plan's ltx-2.5 model.

The spoken ad tool is still the better fit than the talking-photo one, since it generates the speech and lip movement together, but I can't promise every word will sync perfectly. Before committing to it, I'll check the talking-photo workflow guide to be sure I'm not missing a better option.

events.text:
I'm weighing whether a generated spoken-ad video would count as a voiceover, since the user ruled that out and an AI voice from a script looks close to one. I also doubt a generative model can guarantee every word is exact, and the commercial use for "our sale" would need a paid subscription.

I'm settling on telling the user not to generate anything yet. I'd offer two routes: they record their own audio so I can make the talking photo for free, or, if they're fine with an AI voice, the spoken ad with ltx-2.5, though it can't promise exact lip sync. I'll also flag that commercial use needs a paid plan.

I haven't made anything yet, because what you asked for can't be done the way you described it.

**Why:** The tool that makes a photo talk with lips matched to the words needs a recording of the speech. It can't turn text into speech. Since you don't have a recording yet, the only way to get "Welcome to our sale!" from the free tools would be to create a voice first. That's the voiceover you told me not to make, so I stopped here and haven't spent any credits.

**Options:**
1. **Send a recording of yourself saying it (the best fit).** An MP3, WAV or M4A of you saying "Welcome to our sale!" is enough. I'll use it to make the talking-photo video, which runs on the free plan, and give you the download link. The lips are matched to your real audio, so this is the most accurate option.
2. **Let the AI make the voice too (only if you change your mind).** A free tool can make a short video, up to 5 seconds at 480p, where the AI creates both the voice and the lip movement from the text. That's the substitute you ruled out, and I can't promise the lips will match every word. I'll only do this if you ask.

**Before you post it:** Since this is for a sale, it's probably promotional. Magic Hour's terms say commercial use needs a paid plan or a credit-pack purchase. Free-plan videos may not be allowed in ads, so check [their terms](https://magichour.ai/terms-of-service) before using it publicly.

Send the recording and I'll make the video.
